stem: Which criterion defines secondary nocturnal enuresis?

options.text: The child has been dry for over 6 months before wetting starts again
The child has never been dry for more than a few months
The child wets only during high-stress situations
The child has daytime urgency and frequency
The child wets occasionally after recent toilet training

explanation: Secondary nocturnal enuresis is defined by a return of wetting after at least 6 months of dryness.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because secondary nocturnal enuresis requires a previous dry period of more than 6 months before bedwetting returns
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this describes persistent or primary enuresis rather than recurrence after a dry interval
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because stress may contribute to wetting but does not define secondary enuresis
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because daytime urgency and frequency suggest daytime lower urinary tract symptoms, not the definition of secondary nocturnal enuresis
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because recent toilet training with occasional wetting does not meet the definition of secondary nocturnal enuresis

source.hint: Consider the duration of the 'dry' period required to distinguish this from the primary form.
